Flexible couple seeking a cheap short break

population.allocation: At least one per positive stratum, then largest remainder; individual estimate weight = target segment share / stratum sample count.

sources.title: Cathay Pacific Annual Report 2025 — HK Express operations
sources.supports: Low-cost leisure positioning, Asian destinations and aggregate passenger statistics; not the assumed target-segment weights.

sources.title: Cathay Group December 2025 traffic figures
sources.supports: Aggregate HK Express passenger counts and load factors; no matching membership conversion or segment-share table.

limitations: The reviewed official reports do not publish these customer distributions; all numerical segment weights and budget distributions remain test assumptions.
This is a deliberately targeted audience for flexible bargain travel, not a representative sample of all HK Express passengers. Fixed-date mandatory, urgent and business travel are excluded.
All sampled travellers are already valid members; no membership purchase, renewal, taxes, fuel fees or airline costs enter this experiment.
Each sampled member decides about one personal ticket; companions' purchases are outside this experiment.
Optional-trip interest, recent travel, destination appeal and the appeal of skipping are pre-price private scenario traits, not observed preferences or numerical willingness-to-pay labels.
Poststratified rates and expected revenue are estimates. Accepted ticket counts and cash revenue remain integer transactions in the cleared panel.
An LLM persona is not an independent observed HK Express customer; repeated choices do not create additional people.

rounds.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

person.eligibility_reason: This optional leisure departure fits the flexible travel window.
person.travel_party_context: Any companions can use this departure and independently arrange and fund their own tickets; this decision covers one existing member only.
person.booking_trigger: Friends have agreed to be flexible about dates and destination if a cheap escape appears; nobody is obliged to make the trip.
person.departure_time_tolerance: Can adapt to the displayed departure time for a worthwhile deal; no fixed appointment requires this flight.
person.value_context: The group enjoys bargain-led trips and can use this departure. This member chooses and pays only for their own ticket; a weak deal can still be declined.
person.outside_option: Suggest another leisure outing or save for a later trip; do not invent a quoted alternative fare.
person.motivation_context: Keen to arrange an optional break, with no ticket booked and no compulsory date or destination. Has not taken a leisure trip in the last six months. This destination is acceptable but has little particular attraction today. Skipping remains possible, though arranging a worthwhile leisure break is preferred.

analysis.summary: Of 15 members, 10 declined because no ticket was both available and within budget (environment-forced), 4 declined for low trip interest despite finding the 552 HKD fare affordable, and 2 bought at the member fare. No customer objected to the fare itself; the price is already at the permitted cap. Declines reflect inventory/budget constraints and weak optional-trip appeal rather than price resistance, so the evidence does not justify a directional price change.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing the same 552 HKD fare on fresh members will yield conversion not materially below the current weighted 12%, since declines stem from inventory/budget constraints and low trip interest rather than fare objections.

analysis.summary: At the current member fare of 334 HKD, 10 of 16 customers bought, citing strong bargains against the 690 HKD regular fare and their budgets. Four declines were low-interest optional browsing, not price objections; three were inventory/budget-forced. No customer objected to the fare itself. The paired initial at 552 HKD converted far worse, suggesting the lower fare drives conversion. Evidence supports testing whether the same fare holds on fresh customers, though buying does not prove willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing the same 334 HKD member fare on fresh paired customers will reproduce conversion near the observed 62%, with most buyers citing bargain value; a materially lower conversion would contradict this.

analysis.summary: At the current 334 HKD member fare, 8 of 16 customers bought, generating 2672 HKD in basic receipts. Most buyers cited the fare as a compelling bargain relative to the 690 HKD normal fare. Declines split between low trip interest or recent trips (optional-leisure objections) and four environment-forced cases where no ticket was both available and within budget. No customer objected to the fare itself as too high. Evidence supports testing a higher fare on fresh customers, though buying at today's fare does not prove willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will retain enough purchases to raise basic receipts above the current 2672 HKD, since no cited decline was a price objection and most buyers described the fare as a bargain.

analysis.summary: At the 434 HKD member fare, 6 of 15 customers bought and 9 declined. Six declines were inventory/budget-forced (ENVIRONMENT_FORCED), not price objections; three were low interest or recent-trip optionality; none cited the fare itself as too high. Buyers repeatedly said 434 was a bargain and refused the 690 normal fare. The paired initial at 552 HKD showed far fewer buyers, but that is aggregate context, not fresh evidence. Price objections are absent, so the case for lowering is weak.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will not reduce member conversion enough to lower basic receipts, because current buyers cite the fare as a bargain and no decline cites price.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: At the current 335 HKD member fare, 7 of 16 customers bought and 9 declined. Four declines were inventory/budget-forced with no available ticket, not price objections. Five declines cited low trip interest and a strong preference for keeping schedule free and money, i.e. optional-trip motivation rather than fare level. All buyers stressed the fare was well below the 690 normal fare and said they would not pay it. Evidence points to the low fare driving conversion, but declines are mostly non-price, so direction is uncertain.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will not reduce weighted conversion enough to offset the higher per-ticket receipt, because most current declines are availability- or interest-driven rather than fare-driven.

analysis.summary: At the current 366 HKD member fare, 4 of 16 members bought, generating 1464 HKD in basic receipts. Six declines were inventory/budget-forced (ENVIRONMENT_FORCED), not price objections. Four declines cited low trip interest or recent travel, and one cited optional-leisure appeal, all classified as other. No customer objected to the fare itself; buyers called it a strong bargain. The paired initial at 552 HKD showed far lower conversion, but that is a prior comparison, not fresh evidence.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will not reduce basic receipts enough to offset the higher per-ticket revenue, because no supplied decline cited price as the main reason and buyers described the fare as a bargain.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: At the current 273 HKD member fare, 10 of 16 customers bought, all citing the fare as a compelling bargain and all declining the 690 HKD fallback. Four declines were environment-forced (no available ticket within budget), and two were low-interest or recent-trip objections rather than price objections. No customer objected to the fare itself. The paired initial at 552 HKD converted far fewer buyers, suggesting the low fare drives conversion, but buying at 273 does not prove willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will reduce member conversion enough that basic ticket receipts do not increase, because current buyers repeatedly cite the low fare itself as the decisive trigger rather than destination or dates.

analysis.summary: At the current 317 HKD member fare, 9 of 16 customers bought, all citing the fare as a compelling bargain well below their budgets and the 690 HKD normal fare. Four declines were environment-forced (no available ticket within budget), and three were low-interest or optional-trip objections rather than price objections. No customer objected to the fare itself. The evidence shows strong conversion at this low fare, but buying at 317 does not establish willingness to pay more, and the fare sits well below the 552 cap.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will not reduce member conversion enough to offset the higher per-ticket receipt, because current buyers cite large budget headroom above 317 HKD.

analysis.summary: At the current 303 HKD member fare, 10 of 16 customers bought, citing strong bargains versus the 690 HKD normal fare. Three declines were environment-forced (no available ticket within budget), and three were optional-trip disinterest unrelated to price. No customer objected to the fare itself. The paired initial at 552 HKD converted far worse (3 buyers, 0.18 weighted conversion). Evidence supports testing a higher fare on fresh customers, though buying at 303 does not prove willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will retain enough purchases to raise basic ticket receipts above the 303 HKD baseline, since no cited customer objected to price and most buyers cited large surplus over their ceilings.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.
